muayThai.title: Visas for Muay Thai training in Thailand
muayThai.metaTitle: Muay Thai Visa Thailand: DTV vs ED vs Visa Exemption
muayThai.metaDescription: Training Muay Thai in Thailand? Compare the DTV soft-power visa, the ED visa and visa-free entry, and find out what your camp needs to provide.
muayThai.intro: Whether you're training for two weeks or a full year, pick the visa that matches your camp plans.
muayThai.shortText: Short training trips are often possible on visa-free entry (now 30 days for most nationalities), but official guidance on training as 'tourism' is unclear, so check before you book.
muayThai.longText: The DTV covers Muay Thai as a soft-power activity, with long stays and multiple entries. An ED visa from a licensed school is the alternative.
muayThai.tipsTitle: Tips before you book a camp
muayThai.tip1: Ask the camp whether it can issue the enrolment/confirmation letter your visa needs.
muayThai.tip2: Budget for proof of funds as well as camp fees.
muayThai.tip3: Keep your training schedule and receipts in case immigration asks.

nomads.metaTitle: Digital Nomad Visa Thailand: DTV Guide & Best Cities

nomads.intro: The Destination Thailand Visa (DTV) lets remote workers stay for long periods while working for employers and clients outside Thailand.
nomads.chiangMai: Chiang Mai: affordable, calm, big co-working scene.
nomads.bangkok: Bangkok: fast internet, city life, easy flights.
nomads.kohPhangan: Koh Phangan: island living with a nomad community.
nomads.taxNote: Staying 180 days or more in a calendar year can make you a Thai tax resident. Read our digital nomad guide and get tax advice.

business.title: Business visas for Thailand
business.metaTitle: Thailand Business Visa: Non-B, Work Permits, LTR & SMART
business.metaDescription: Meetings, jobs and investment in Thailand: when the visa exemption is enough, and when you need a Non-B, work permit, LTR or SMART visa.
business.intro: From a few meetings to a long-term job or investment, here's which visa matches your plans.
business.meetingsText: Since 15 September 2026, visa-free entry is for tourism only. For meetings or conferences, check whether you need a Non-Immigrant B visa. Working always requires a work permit.
business.workText: You need a Non-Immigrant B visa and a work permit arranged with your employer.
business.talentText: The LTR and SMART visas offer long stays and perks for qualifying professionals and investors.
